items.title: Training Cognition SWE-1.7: Asynchronous RL at Global Scale
items.summary: This talk covers the systems and algorithmic challenges behind making globally distributed RL work at scale. We will discuss how we decouple training from inference, propagate compressed weight updates across datacenters, control policy staleness, and design the infrastructure to tolerate frequent hardware failures. We will also examine the training–inference mismatches that emerge in asynchronous RL and the techniques we use to preserve policy entropy and maintain stable learning over long training runs.

items.title: Claude Haiku 5.5: Anthropic's New Workhorse.
items.summary: Anthropic just released Claude Haiku 5.5, which it calls its cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model yet. For prompts under 100,000 tokens, it costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens. That's 90% less than Haiku 4.5 and the same price as OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna. Above 100K tokens it's half off, and Anthropic estimates typical workloads cost about 75% less. On OSWorld 2.1, a computer-use benchmark, Anthropic reports 72.4%, up from 15.7% for Haiku 4.5. It's also the first Haiku with an adjustable effort setting. Anthropic positions it as a workhorse for summaries, classification, and subagent jobs alongside Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, and says the bigger models are still the better choice for complex agentic coding. All benchmark numbers are Anthropic's own; independent results aren't in yet. Also announced: Sonnet 5.5 cache reads are now half price. Max and Team plans get monthly API credits, rolling out this week: $100 on Max 5x, $200 on Max 20x, and up to $500 pooled on Team. Available today on the Claude API, AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure as claude-haiku-5-5. Sources: Anthropic announcement: https://www.anthropic.com/claude-haiku-5-5 Models overview: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview VentureBeat: https://venturebeat.com/technology/anthropic-launches-claude-haiku-5-5-with-90-api-price-reduction-matching-gpt-6-luna #ClaudeHaiku #Claude #Anthropic #AI #LLM #Shorts

items.title: From World Models to Working Machines: Physical AI in the Real World
items.summary: Construction and mining sites are among the hardest environments on earth for autonomy. Heavy machines, unpredictable terrain, and no tolerance for failure. Foundation models and world models are changing what's possible in robotics, and industrial equipment is where those advances meet their toughest test. Caterpillar and NVIDIA join CoreWeave for a conversation on physical AI at industrial scale: what recent advances make feasible today that weren't a few years ago, what changes when AI leaves the lab and enters safety-critical environments, how simulation and synthetic data close the loop between virtual and physical, and what compute, infrastructure, and partnerships it will take to move from proof of concept to fleets in the field.

items.title: Fueling Innovation at Scale: Inside Pinterest’s Machine Learning Platform
items.summary: You'll leave this session knowing what mature model lifecycle management actually looks like, and what it takes to get there. Pinterest's ML platform team will share how they think about the full lifecycle, training, registration, artifact packaging, deployment, and serving, and the milestones that mark real progress along the way. Their migration to Weights & Biases (W&B Models) is part of that story, including what changed, what got easier, and what challenges came with it, but the session is really about the broader journey, not just the move itself. You'll walk away with a perspective on what to prioritize as your own model lifecycle matures, and the tradeoffs Pinterest weighed at each stage.

items.title: Building the Voice OS at Willow
items.summary: What does it take to build voice AI that hundreds of thousands of people can use across their everyday applications? Accurate speech recognition is only the beginning, with the real challenge making the output fast, reliable, and personalized. In this session, Lawrence, Co-Founder and CTO of Willow Voice, shares the engineering and product lessons behind building voice AI at scale spanning supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and personalization. The session then examines personalization in-depth: establishing good defaults, learning from user corrections, and turning subjective writing preferences into behaviors a model can follow. Attendees will leave with lessons applicable to building specialized AI products well beyond voice.

items.summary: From building PyTorch into the world's leading open-source AI framework to leading the Llama open-source initiative at Meta, Joe Spisak has spent his career at the center of the open AI movement. items.title: Introducing OpenDocRouter: Call any OCR model in a single line of code
items.summary: OpenDocRouter turns PDFs and images into clean markdown using the latest frontier and open-source OCR models, including Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash, GPT-6 Luna, MinerU2.5-Pro and PaddleOCR-VL. Switching models means changing one parameter. You don't touch prompts, rate limits or deployments. Every model is benchmarked on ParseBench for both quality and cost. Turn on layout and any model returns grounded bounding boxes with the same set of layout classes, even models that can't do this natively. Billing is pay-per-token, starting as low as $0.80 per 1,000 pages, and you aren't charged for pages that fail. ▶ Try it: https://www.opendocrouter.ai/ ▶ Docs: https://www.opendocrouter.ai/docs ▶ Models + benchmarks: https://www.opendocrouter.ai/models ▶ Launch blog: https://www.llamaindex.ai/blog/introducing-opendocrouter

He recounts a painful personal experience where AI inserted made-up references into his work, leading to reputational damage and a judge questioning the credibility of his entire declaration. This incident highlights the challenges and risks associated with AI, even for those with extensive expertise in the field.

items.title: AI Models vs. AI Decisions: What Enterprises Need to Know
items.summary: Over the past 12 months, enterprise AI strategy has shifted from simply building models and deploying experimental agents to integrating AI directly into core business processes that drive measurable ROI. As organizations face ballooning token costs from over-relying on frontier LLMs for routine tasks, enterprise leaders are pivoting toward Small Language Models (SLMs), building semantic ontology layers to give agents enterprise context, and implementing AI-native harness engineering for production-ready code. In this interview recorded live at Cypher 2026, Senior Tech Journalist Supreeth Koundinya sits down with Rashmi Tambe, VP & Head of AI Product Engineering at Tredence. She breaks down the evolving role of developers from "vibe coding" to harness engineering, why the enterprise data context problem is becoming a semantic/ontology challenge, deploying SLM gateways to optimize token spend, returning to classic machine learning fundamentals, and measuring success through business outcomes rather than agent count. items.title: Stop Brain Drain: The Strategy to Build Deep Tech in India
items.summary: While Indian academic institutions generate world-class deep-tech research, translating lab-stage innovations into viable, commercialized market products remains a key hurdle. Established under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, Technology Innovation Hubs (TIHs) at premier institutes like IIT Bombay bridge this gap by funding seed-stage startups, advancing physical AI systems, and converting academic intellectual property into industry-ready solutions. In this interview recorded live at Cypher 2026, Sudhi Sachdev speaks with Dhruti Pillai, Assistant Vice President (AVP) of Technology at TIH, IIT Bombay. They explore reversing the traditional tech "brain drain" in favor of indigenous innovation, funding early-stage founders in physical AI, navigating enterprise procurement and corporate adoption risks, balancing ground-level reality with government policy, and leveraging frugal innovation to build sovereign technology capabilities for India. items.title: Why 80% of AI Projects Never Scale | Ankur Rai, Straive | CYPHER 2026

The primary bottleneck lies not in model intelligence, but in moving from initial feasibility pilots to operationalized scale, a transition that requires data context engineering, intelligence hierarchy optimization, workflow redesign, and output verification. items.title: LLM Applications: Conversational AI, Document Intelligence & Text-to-SQL
items.summary: Language models are not just a chat technology. The same capability reads your documents and queries your databases. Terms covered: - Conversational AI: multi-turn dialogue that remembers context, handles follow-ups, adapts to intent and escalates when it hits its limits - Document Extraction: pulling structured information out of contracts, invoices, claims, medical records and filings, in seconds instead of hours - Text-to-SQL: asking a database a question in plain English and getting the answer back, with no technical intermediary and no waiting on a data team Conversation, documents and data. Three very different surfaces, made accessible through the same underlying capability. — AI Fundamentals Glossary | H2O.ai University Full playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWKlIKS-66E Free courses and certifications: https://h2o.ai/university #ConversationalAI #DocumentAI #TextToSQL #AIGlossary #H2Oai
